gaps.text: In-line measurement of temperature at the measurement point with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion level: start with one model per method, then join the two blocks (block-scaled spectra or extracted scores) so that the block with more variables does not dominate. Both probes must look at the same small spot and the two data streams must be brought to a common time step, with a separate calibration and diagnostic kept for each instrument. Keep the fused model only if it beats the best single method on independent runs.)
Whether Raman, NIR or a fused model can distinguish the crystal forms of interest in a continuous crystalliser; no crystallisation, polymorph or solute-concentration case is supplied.
Any accuracy, precision, detection-limit or response-time figures for solute concentration or crystal form.

items.finding: In a continuous reactive extraction study using FT-IR and Raman, temperature was varied together with acid concentrations and ionic strength to obtain a robust model.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests temperature should be considered as a varying factor when building calibrations, which may inform whether and how to measure temperature at the probe location.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The study is on liquid-liquid extraction in lithium recycling, not crystallisation, and it does not describe an in-line temperature sensor or probe-level measurement.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
citation.label: E03 ¶19

items.finding: A review states that before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: This supports testing each probe's contribution and complementarity before deciding whether a fused Raman-NIR model is worth keeping.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: It is a review statement, not a crystallisation or Raman/NIR case, and it does not give a procedure for common time steps or same-spot alignment.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E02 ¶82

items.finding: In a textile hyperspectral imaging study, low-level data fusion concatenated fluorescence and reflectance blocks along the spectral dimension after separate block autoscaling.
items.how_it_applies: This illustrates separate block scaling before concatenation, which could inform how to prevent one Raman or NIR block from dominating a fused model.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The application is dyed textiles with hyperspectral imaging, not in-line Raman/NIR in a crystalliser, and the fusion is not tested for solute concentration or crystal form.

citation.quote: As the final step, a low-level data fusion method was chosen to merge F- and R-block by concatenating them along the spectral dimension after separate block autoscaling.
citation.label: E05 ¶20
